newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait warns Gulf Arabs of an "external danger".
newsitem.headline: Kuwait warns Gulf Arabs of an "external danger".

text.p: Kuwait's Crown Prince Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah on Wednesday warned fellow Arabs in the oil-rich Gulf region of an unspecified expansionist external danger.

"The real danger that threatens the security and stability of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states is an external danger," said Sheikh Saad, whose country is a member of the GCC along with Saudi Arabia, Oman, Bahrain, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates.

"It (danger) stems from greed, domination and expansion tendencies," Sheikh Saad, also Pirme Minister, said in a speech at the opening session of the tiny state's planning council carried by the official Kuwait News Agency.
Sheikh Saad did not specify the source of the danger.
U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry on Friday said non-Arab Iran and former Kuwait occupier Iraq sought control of two-thirds of the world's oil supplies located in the Gulf.

Although some diplomats say Washington had at times overstated any threat from Iran, several Western powers and Gulf Arab states have in the past few months expressed concern over Tehran's growing military might.
Iran is strategically placed at the only entrance to the Gulf, the narrow Strait of Hormuz through which 15 million barrels of oil pass daily.

GCC countries should "unify their ranks and word" to face this danger, Sheikh Saad said. The GCC is to hold its annual summit in the Qatar on December 7. Bahrain has said it will skip the meeting due to a territorial dispute with Qatar.
"None of the GCC countries is far or safe from this external danger," he said.

Sheikh Saad reiterated Iraq remains to be a threat to his country. "The Iraqi regime still poses a threat to our homeland and the safety of our people and did not abandon its expansionist plans and evil intentions."
"We ought to maintain constant caution and vigilance and monitor the enemy's every move."
Iraq annexed Kuwait as its 19th province in August 1990 for seven months. A U.S.-led coalition drove Iraq's occupation troops from Kuwait after a six-week offensive.
